title: The Timber Giants
text: Trees rise so tall their tops are lost in mist, their trunks wide as towers, their bark ridged like old skin. A single one would roof a House. The woodfolk say they are sleeping. In the hush you can hear them breathe.

options.label: The strongest fells one of the giants.

outcomes.text: It falls with a sound like a groan. The others stir.

options.label: Take only what has fallen and let the giants sleep.

outcomes.text: There is enough, and the woodfolk nod.

options.label: Ask the woodfolk for a gift, rather than take one.

outcomes.text: They give you a branch of their oldest tree. It is still breathing.
